transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Oh, hello Dr. Smith. It's so nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really hope I'm not taking time away from your more serious patients. 

Well, um... I guess I'm here because my family thought it might be good to just... check in. It's probably nothing, really, just... I feel like I’m always up and moving. Even on what's supposed to be a quiet day at home, I just sort of... well, I end up bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag, and then over to some travel papers... usually before I’ve really finished any one thing. 

I try to tell myself that keeping busy at my age is a good thing, right? But I suppose it does get a little exhausting never really settling down, and my daughter worries. Is that the sort of thing you help people with? I hope I'm explaining it alright...
Have you always been this way for as long as you can remember, or is this 'bouncing around' something that started more recently?

Oh, my... well, I suppose it's not entirely new. I've always been a bit of a busy bee, you know? 

I hope it's alright to go all the way back to when I was a little girl, but... well, even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a very bright child, just... maybe a little scattered. I didn't mean any harm by it, of course! But I was always misplacing my school papers, or accidentally talking out of turn when I got excited about a lesson. And they said I was always wiggling around in my seat before I actually finished my assignments. 

Just full of energy, I guess! I always tried my very best to be a good student and not be a bother to the teachers, I really did. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question properly...
Have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where your mood was unusually high, or where you felt you had so much energy that you didn't need much sleep at all?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I mean, I certainly have my energetic days, like I mentioned, but... well, I always make sure to get my rest. 

I wouldn't say my mood is ever unusually high, either. I try to stay cheerful and positive, of course, because nobody likes a grump, right? But I've never felt like I was, oh, I don't know, out of control or anything like that. I've always been a very sensible person, I hope. And I definitely need my sleep! If I don't get my seven or eight hours, I'm just no good to anyone the next day. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I've ever had days like what you're describing. I hope that's a good thing? I'm trying to be as helpful as I can...
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your time feeling worried or anxious about various things in your daily life, such as your health, your family, or your responsibilities?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say a *significant* amount of time, no. I mean, I think it's perfectly normal for a mother and grandmother to care about her family, don't you think? 

I suppose I do think about whether everyone is doing alright, and I want to make sure I'm keeping up with my little daily tasks so I'm not a burden to anyone. But I wouldn't call it... well, I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person. I try to just take things one day at a time and keep a smile on my face. Worrying doesn't really solve anything, does it? 

I hope I don't sound like a fretful old lady! I just care about my loved ones, that's all. Does that sound like a normal amount of worry to you? I really do try to just be positive about things.

When you are working on those tasks you mentioned, like your gardening list or your knitting, do you find that you often struggle to keep your focus on the task until it is completely finished, or do you find yourself frequently distracted by other things?

Oh, well... I suppose I do get a little sidetracked sometimes. Not on purpose, of course! I always mean to finish what I start. 

Like with my knitting, or... well, even when I'm just trying to pay attention at the church planning meetings. I'll start out listening so carefully, really trying to take it all in, but then... I don't know, my mind just sort of wanders off for a bit. And before I know it, I realize I've missed half of what was said. Or even if I'm just reading the church bulletin, I'll find I haven't really taken in the words. 

I feel so terrible when it happens, because I really do want to be involved and helpful! I just... I suppose I lose my place a little. But I always try to catch back up! Is that... is that the sort of thing you mean? I hope I don't sound too scatterbrained...

In those situations where you are expected to sit still for a longer period, like at a movie, a long church service, or perhaps while traveling, do you find it physically difficult or uncomfortable to remain in your seat?

Oh, well... I do try my very best to be polite and sit quietly, especially during a sermon. I certainly wouldn't want to be a distraction to anyone! But... I suppose, if I have to sit still for too long, I do start to get this... oh, this sort of stirred-up feeling inside. 

It's hard to explain, really. It's just this little urge where I feel like I need to stand up and, I don't know, straighten something up or go check on something in the other room. Even if I'm just watching a nice movie, my mind will tell me there's a cushion that needs fluffing or a pot on the stove I should peek at. 

I usually just try to shift in my seat or adjust my purse so I don't bother anyone around me. I'm sure that's just a normal part of being a homemaker for so many years, don't you think? You just get so used to being on your feet and keeping things tidy. I hope it doesn't make me sound terribly fidgety or rude... I really do try my best to be a good listener! Does that make sense to you?
In your day-to-day life, do you find that you frequently lose or misplace items you need to get things done, like your keys, glasses, or important paperwork?

Oh, goodness, no... I don't think I have much trouble with that at all. I try to be very careful with my things, I really do. 

I've always kept a little glass dish right by the front door for my keys, so I always know exactly where they are. And my important papers go straight into a special drawer in the den. I would just hate to be one of those people who is always losing things and making everyone else run around looking for them! 

I mean, I suppose every now and then I might leave my reading glasses on the kitchen counter instead of the coffee table, but... well, that's just normal for someone my age, isn't it? I always find them right away. I really do try my best to keep everything organized and in its proper place so I don't cause any fuss. I hope that's the sort of answer you were looking for?
Do you find that you often interrupt others while they are speaking, or perhaps blurt out answers before someone has finished their question, even when you try to be polite?

Oh, goodness... well, I certainly try my hardest to be polite at all times. Good manners are just so important, don't you agree? 

But... I suppose... well, my husband does mention sometimes that I cut him off before he's quite finished speaking. And... oh, I feel a little embarrassed to admit this, but I suppose I do the same thing at my church group planning meetings, too. 

I really don't ever mean to be rude or pushy! It's just that... well, a thought will pop into my head about whatever we're discussing, and I get so worried I'll completely lose the thought if I don't say it right then and there. I just sort of let it out so it doesn't slip away from me. 

I always try to apologize the moment I realize I've spoken out of turn. I just hate the idea of offending anyone... I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly ill-mannered? Do you think people understand I'm just trying to be helpful and contribute to the conversation?

You mentioned feeling this way both at home and at your church meetings; do you find that these difficulties with staying focused or feeling restless create significant problems for you in those settings, such as feeling frustrated or having others express concern about your behavior?

Oh, well... I certainly wouldn't want to complain or make a mountain out of a molehill. I try so hard to be useful, you know. But... oh dear, I suppose I should be completely honest with you. 

It... well, it has started causing some real strain lately. At home, and over at the community center, too. I just feel so terribly embarrassed even saying it out loud. It’s just that my husband, bless his heart, and the other volunteers... well, they’ve realized they can’t really count on me to keep our plans straight anymore unless someone is checking behind me. 

I just hate being a burden or making extra work for anyone else! I really do try my very best to keep everything organized, I promise. It's just awful when you feel like you're letting people down and they have to double-check your work, isn't it? I hope you don't think too poorly of me for it... I really am trying to do better. Do you think it's something I can fix?

Looking back at your life, would you say that the difficulties with staying focused and organized have been more of a constant struggle for you than the feelings of restlessness and the tendency to interrupt others?

Oh, my... well, I wouldn't say one was necessarily more of a struggle than the other, if I'm being completely honest. I hope it's alright to say that? 

It's a little embarrassing to look back on, because I always wanted to be such a good girl for my parents, but... well, it seems like both of those things have been with me for a very, very long time. Even way back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl—which was lovely of them to say, of course—but... they also said I was terribly scattered. 

I was always losing my school papers, and... oh dear, talking out of turn, just like I was mentioning earlier. And I just couldn't seem to stop wiggling around in my seat before my work was even finished. 

I really did try my hardest to sit still and be a good student, I promise! I just had so much nervous energy, and my mind was always going a mile a minute. I hope I don't sound like I was a dreadful child? I always meant well, I truly did. Does that help answer your question?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a lifelong pattern of inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms that are consistent with ADHD. Symptoms such as difficulty sustaining attention, physical restlessness, and impulsive speech were present in childhood and persist in adulthood, causing functional impairment in social and domestic settings.
